title: More than Classification: A Unified Framework for Event Temporal Relation Extraction
research_question: Can event temporal relation extraction be improved and made more transferable by representing relation labels as logical constraints over event start and end points rather than as independent one-hot classes?
methodology: The authors first construct a strong pretrained-language-model baseline using event markers, extended sentence context, label-symmetry augmentation, an MLP classifier, and cross-entropy training. Their unified framework instead interprets each temporal label as a logical expression over four cross-event endpoint pairs and predicts endpoint relations by answering two binary ordering questions for each pair. Soft logic makes the rule-based conversion differentiable so that the whole framework can be trained from event-relation labels. Experiments use TB-Dense and MATRES with BERT-Base and RoBERTa-Large, followed by error, low-resource, and cross-definition transfer analyses.

key_findings.finding: The unified endpoint framework consistently improves over the enhanced direct-classification baseline and reaches 68.1 micro-F1 on TB-Dense and 82.6 on MATRES with RoBERTa-Large, reported as 0.3 F1 above the previous state of the art on both benchmarks.

Explicit logical treatment of the Vague relation substantially reduces confusion with Vague: the number of Vague-associated errors falls by 95 on TB-Dense and 22 on MATRES, although non-Vague errors increase slightly.
The unified representation is more data-efficient in low-resource TB-Dense experiments, averaging gains of 2.9 micro-F1 and 1.8 macro-F1 over the baseline across training subsets from 1% to 30%.
When trained on TB-Dense and evaluated under MATRES relation definitions, the unified model obtains 70.4 micro-F1 versus 63.1 and 64.3 for two baseline label-mapping strategies.
Gains occur with both BERT-Base and RoBERTa-Large, suggesting that the endpoint decomposition contributes beyond the choice of text encoder.

limitations: The authors explicitly evaluate only TB-Dense and MATRES and state that more relation inventories and datasets are needed to establish generalization and robustness.
The experiments concern event-pair temporal relations rather than end-to-end detection of evolving work-item states.

The framework does not directly represent factuality distinctions such as planned, confirmed, revoked, completed, or contradicted; such distinctions would require additional semantics beyond endpoint ordering.
The evaluated input context is local text around supplied event mentions, leaving cross-document or long-running communication histories outside the demonstrated setting.
raw_claims: Standard temporal-relation classification discards semantic structure by treating relation labels as independent categories.
The framework represents event intervals through their start and end points.
Four cross-event endpoint pairs are sufficient for the temporal interpretations used by the framework.
Two binary questions are used to distinguish before, after, equal, and vague relations between time points.
Soft logic provides a differentiable mapping from endpoint judgments to event-level temporal labels.
TB-Dense uses six evaluated relation types while MATRES focuses on four start-point relations.
The unified model improves over its matched enhanced baseline on both evaluated datasets.
Logical interpretation reduces many errors in which non-Vague instances are predicted as Vague.
Sharing endpoint structure among relation labels improves performance when training data are limited.
Changing the logical conversion rules permits transfer between different temporal-relation definitions without learning a new one-to-one label mapping.
